newsitem.title: USA: Time Warner Cable pleased with Fox stance.
newsitem.headline: Time Warner Cable pleased with Fox stance.

text.p: Time Warner Cable, a unit of Time Warner Inc, said on Wednesday it is "pleased" that News Corp Ltd's Fox television has stopped insisting that several cable systems should remove Fox network programs from their channel line-ups on January 1.

"We are confident the court will agree with us that our existing Fox contracts give Time Warner Cable the right to continue carrying Fox signals from the stations they are purchasing from New World (Communications Group Inc )," the company said in a written statement.

Fox's stance is a temporary resolution to a legal dispute regarding the rights of Time Warner Cable to retransmit Fox's programming at the former New World stations. The stations are in Tampa, Fla., Milwaukee, Wis., Austin, Texas, Detroit and Kansas City and affect about 1.5 million subscribers, the company said.

Time Warner Cable said it was not clear if Fox's stance would help end the ongoing dispute between the companies. The current resolution is good for 45 days, the company said, and a lawsuit continues in Tampa on this issue.
